entries.note: Co-written with Ernest Davis in the authors' shared 'we' voice. Which part of theory of mind is 'most important' is a judgment that has no agreed public test.

entries.test: Whether successive released versions of LLMs and MT systems score higher overall on benchmarks yet get specific items wrong that earlier versions got right (e.g., documented version-to-version regressions).
entries.note: The aside that unimproved versions aren't released is part of what he claims, but it adds no condition. The 'conditions' field lists scope rather than real antecedents.

entries.test: Data-contamination or memorization studies showing that published test examples, including those from Marcus and Davis, appear in or are reproduced from LLM training data.
entries.note: Only the training-data part is firm. The benchmark part is hedged with 'perhaps' and should not be graded.
